declarations.name: Applications.Sorting.sorters_eq_at
declarations.source_header:
theorem sorters_eq_at (r : α → α → Prop) [Std.Antisymm r]
    (f g : List α → List α) (xs : List α)
    (hf : (f xs).Pairwise r ∧ (f xs).Perm xs)
    (hg : (g xs).Pairwise r ∧ (g xs).Perm xs) : f xs = g xs
declarations.assessment: Arbitrary Type u, Prop-valued relation and arbitrary list functions; only Std.Antisymm r. Hypotheses concern the actual two returned lists at the supplied input. Perm composition is f(xs) ~ xs ~ g(xs), followed by standard list uniqueness. No universal sorter existence is asserted for a non-total relation.

declarations.name: Applications.Sorting.sorters_eq
declarations.source_header:
theorem sorters_eq (r : α → α → Prop) [Std.Antisymm r]
    (f g : List α → List α)
    (hf : ∀ xs, (f xs).Pairwise r ∧ (f xs).Perm xs)
    (hg : ∀ xs, (g xs).Pairwise r ∧ (g xs).Perm xs) : f = g
declarations.assessment: Both correctness specifications quantify over every List α before the function-equality conclusion. Uses the local public theorem at each input and funext. No stability, decisibility, totality, transitivity, payload equality/default or execution/cost contract is introduced.

declarations.name: Applications.Sorting.sorters_eq_of_multiset
declarations.source_header:
theorem sorters_eq_of_multiset (r : α → α → Prop) [Std.Antisymm r]
    (f g : List α → List α)
    (hf : ∀ xs, (f xs).Pairwise r ∧ (f xs : Multiset α) = (xs : Multiset α))
    (hg : ∀ xs, (g xs).Pairwise r ∧ (g xs : Multiset α) = (xs : Multiset α)) :
    f = g
declarations.assessment: Literal source preservation equality is on full Multiset α, not support or cardinality. Each equality converts through the standard iff to Perm; then the universal public result gives function equality. Any input specialization follows with congrFun.

declarations.name: Examples.SortUniqueness.first_pivot_eq_floor
declarations.source_header:
theorem first_pivot_eq_floor [LinearOrder α] :
    quickSortOn (id : α → α) = sortFloorOn (id : α → α)
declarations.assessment: Every LinearOrder element type in Type u; the actual independently defined first-pivot and floor-left source algorithms supply universal sortedness and occurrence witnesses. Their equality is a value-function result only.

declarations.name: Examples.SortUniqueness.three_way_eq_floor
declarations.source_header:
theorem three_way_eq_floor [LinearOrder α] :
    (threeWayQuickSort : List α → List α) = sortFloorOn (id : α → α)
declarations.assessment: Actual three-tail-filter source sorter versus actual contiguous floor-left sorter. Uses the public multiset theorem and floor permutation observation in the new multiset interface. No distinctness premise; all pivot/equal occurrences remain.

declarations.name: Examples.SortUniqueness.floor_mixed_duplicates
declarations.assessment: Exact retained input [2,3,1,2,0,3,2,1] and independent expected output [0,1,1,2,2,2,3,3]. The public new function equality transfers the previously checked mixed_value; no expected value is invented or changed.

declarations.name: Examples.SortUniqueness.reverse_eq_of_equal
declarations.source_header:
theorem reverse_eq_of_equal (xs : List α)
    (hs : xs.Pairwise (fun a b => a = b)) : xs.reverse = xs
declarations.assessment: Generic payload Type u with no instances. An explicit local equality-relation antisymmetry value is declared with ordinary let, following the pinned linter guidance. The actual input is pairwise equal, the reverse observation comes from pairwise_reverse/imp, and standard reverse_perm supplies occurrences. Applies the new pointwise result.

declarations.name: Examples.SortUniqueness.equality_order_boundary
declarations.source_header:
theorem equality_order_boundary :
    (∀ a b : Bool, a = b → b = a → a = b) ∧
      ¬ (∀ a b : Bool, a = b ∨ b = a) ∧
      ([false, false] : List Bool).reverse = [false, false]
declarations.assessment: Closed Bool equality is antisymmetric but not total. The repeated nonempty list has a satisfied pairwise-equality premise and consumes reverse_eq_of_equal. This is not a claim that equality can sort all Bool inputs.

declarations.name: Examples.SortUniqueness.constant_key_boundary
declarations.source_header:
theorem constant_key_boundary :
    (∀ xs : List Bool,
      KeySorted (fun _ : Bool => (0 : Nat)) xs ∧ xs.Perm xs) ∧
    (∀ xs : List Bool,
      KeySorted (fun _ : Bool => (0 : Nat)) xs.reverse ∧ xs.reverse.Perm xs) ∧
    (id : List Bool → List Bool) ≠ List.reverse ∧
    ¬ Stable (fun _ : Bool => (0 : Nat)) [false, true] [false, true].reverse
declarations.assessment: Identity and reverse each satisfy the ordinary key-order/permutation contract for every List Bool, so the boundary is not vacuous. Functions differ on [false,true]. The same reversal violates the complete equal-key filter at key zero. No keyed stability theorem is weakened.
